question: At system scale, what does a capacity analysis for a sanitary collection system mainly compare?
correctAnswer: Peak flows in each sewershed against the rated capacity of downstream pipes and stations
explanation: A capacity analysis compares expected peak flows with the capacity of downstream pipes and stations to find where the system runs out of room.
options: Daily water billing totals against the monthly operating budgets for each maintenance district
Peak flows in each sewershed against the rated capacity of downstream pipes and stations
Crew overtime hours against planned vacation schedules for each operations work group
Pump run time totals against spare parts inventory levels for each individual lift station
optionA: Daily water billing totals against the monthly operating budgets for each maintenance district
optionB: Peak flows in each sewershed against the rated capacity of downstream pipes and stations
optionC: Crew overtime hours against planned vacation schedules for each operations work group
optionD: Pump run time totals against spare parts inventory levels for each individual lift station
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: What is the main purpose of a flow monitoring program in a wastewater collection system?
correctAnswer: To measure flows at selected points so system behaviour can be quantified and compared over time
explanation: Flow monitoring measures flows at chosen locations so the system response can be quantified, compared between areas, and tracked over time.
options: To replace field inspections with a single permanent gauge at the treatment plant inlet
To record rainfall totals at the operations yard for use in monthly activity reporting
To measure flows at selected points so system behaviour can be quantified and compared over time
To count pump starts at each lift station for use in routine maintenance scheduling
optionA: To replace field inspections with a single permanent gauge at the treatment plant inlet
optionB: To record rainfall totals at the operations yard for use in monthly activity reporting
optionC: To measure flows at selected points so system behaviour can be quantified and compared over time
optionD: To count pump starts at each lift station for use in routine maintenance scheduling

question: In a condition grading program, what does a structural grade for a sewer pipe segment describe?
correctAnswer: The severity of defects that affect the pipe strength and its ability to carry loads
explanation: A structural grade rates defects such as cracks and deformation that affect pipe strength and load carrying ability.
options: The severity of defects that affect the pipe strength and its ability to carry loads
The age of the pipe material compared with other pipes installed in the same decade
The number of service connections that drain into the segment from nearby properties
The depth of flow measured in the pipe during the most recent dry weather survey
optionA: The severity of defects that affect the pipe strength and its ability to carry loads
optionB: The age of the pipe material compared with other pipes installed in the same decade
optionC: The number of service connections that drain into the segment from nearby properties
optionD: The depth of flow measured in the pipe during the most recent dry weather survey

question: A trunk sewer runs near capacity during storms while upstream branches still have room. Where does the capacity constraint most likely sit?
correctAnswer: In the downstream trunk reach that carries the combined flow from all upstream branches
explanation: Flows accumulate as branches join, so a downstream trunk reach carrying the combined flow can limit the whole upstream area.
options: In the smallest upstream branch that serves a single short residential side street
In the downstream trunk reach that carries the combined flow from all upstream branches
In the maintenance yard where crews store cleaning and inspection equipment supplies
In the billing system that records customer accounts for the connected service area
optionA: In the smallest upstream branch that serves a single short residential side street
optionB: In the downstream trunk reach that carries the combined flow from all upstream branches
optionC: In the maintenance yard where crews store cleaning and inspection equipment supplies
optionD: In the billing system that records customer accounts for the connected service area

question: CCTV crews in different districts grade the same pipe defect in different ways. What program step best improves grading consistency?

explanation: A shared coding standard, coder training, and audit samples across crews are what make grades comparable across a whole program.

Ask each district to keep its own grading habits so local experience shapes the results
Grade every defect twice and record the higher of the two grades in the asset register
Stop coding minor defects so crews can focus their attention on the largest failures
